newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germans go on trial for attack on two Italians.
newsitem.headline: Germans go on trial for attack on two Italians.

text.p: A German court on Monday began the trial of two young men charged with attempted murder for an attack on two Italian building workers which left one paralysed and barely able to speak.
Prosecutors said the suspects, both in their early 20s, followed the Italians and then attacked them last September in the eastern town of Trebbin.

Prosecutors said the main suspect, 22-year-old Jan Weicht, beat one of the Italians over the head with a baseball bat, leaving him paralysed and only partially able to talk. The other man suffered a broken nose and several broken ribs.
The defence said prosecutors and police had treated their clients unfairly and bent to public pressure in assuming the attack was racist.
The suspects said they had merely acted in self-defence after the Italians threatened them and one threw a stone.

Last December a court in Potsdam, near Berlin, jailed two Germans for a racist attack on three black British construction workers which left one of them paralysed. Germany saw a wave of racist violence after unification in 1990, particularly in the former communist east of the country.
